title: Resolve client IP outside Vercel via WISHSCENE_TRUSTED_PROXIES
context: Better Auth 1.7.6 getIPFromHeader trusts X-Forwarded-For only when it holds exactly one address, unless advanced.ipAddress.trustedProxies is set; otherwise the request falls into one shared 'no-trusted-ip' bucket per path (sign-in DoS for users behind appending proxies). Vercel sets x-real-ip, which is used there.
decision: On Vercel read x-real-ip and ignore trusted proxies. Elsewhere read x-forwarded-for with trustedProxies from WISHSCENE_TRUSTED_PROXIES (comma-separated IPs/CIDRs, validated with node:net isIP + prefix range). A malformed entry keeps product mode disabled (listed in missing). Without the variable, a single-value header works; a multi-value header falls back to Better Auth's shared bucket (documented, warned once by Better Auth).
consequences: Operators behind appending proxies must set WISHSCENE_TRUSTED_PROXIES or share one rate-limit bucket.
Entries Better Auth's parseCIDR rejects are silently dropped by Better Auth, which fails toward 'no IP', not toward trusting a spoofed hop.
alternatives_rejected: Fail closed (reject sign-in) whenever no IP resolves: needs a custom Better Auth hook and blocks legitimate deployments behind overwriting proxies.
Hop-count header rewriting (take Nth from right into a private header): more code, spoofing pitfalls, no current non-Vercel deployment needs it.
Require WISHSCENE_TRUSTED_PROXIES on every non-Vercel deploy: platform proxy CIDRs are often unknown/unstable.
